# Lab 1 

## Q1

Create a code chunk below this question and print the statement:
"`My name is (your name) and my UID is (your UID). I am looking forward to Stats 10!`"

```{r} 
print("My name is Kevin Sheng and my UID is 406-196-414. I am looking forward to Stats 10!")
```

## Q2

Create a vector named `titles` and fill it with at least 3 book
titles. Print the vector `titles`.

```{r}
titles <- c("Bleak House", "Farenheit 451", "Call of the Wild")
print(titles)
```

## Q3

Run the code chunk below using `titles`. Read the error message and
explain why an error occurs.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
sum(titles)
```

ANSWER: `sum()` expects a vector of summable items, or elements for which addition as an operation
makes sense. R doesn't know how to add `character`s, so it throws an error.

## Q4

Create a vector named vector_log and make it hold the values TRUE,
FALSE, TRUE, FALSE. Try multiplying the values by 2 and using the
mean() function. Explain your results and how R treats logical
values.

```{r}
vector_log <- c(TRUE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE)

vector_log2 <- vector_log * 2 # multiplying the values by 2

mean(vector_log)
```

EXPLAIN: `vector_log2` has numerical values while `mean(vector_log)` returns `0.5`.
This seems to indicate that under the hood, `TRUE` and `FALSE` map to `0` and `1` respectively.

## Q5

You are given a vector containing the scores of 50 students on a
recent exam. Find the minimum, maximum, mean, and standard deviation
of the scores. Print each value (for example, print "Mean: \_\_\_").

```{r}
# You do not have to change this code
set.seed(123456789)
scores <- sample(0:100, 50, replace = TRUE)
print(scores)
```

```{r}
# min
sprintf("Minimum: %d", min(scores))

# max
sprintf("Maximum: %d", max(scores))

# mean
sprintf("Mean: %f", mean(scores))

# sd
sprintf("SD: %f", sd(scores))
```

## Q6

Using the `scores` vector, find the mean value without using the `mean()` function. (Hint: The mean is calculated by finding the sum of all values and dividing by the total number of values.)

```{r}
# the sum of all values and dividing by the total number of values
other_mean <- sum(scores) / length(scores)
sprintf("Mean: %f", other_mean)
```

Explain whether there is a difference between the means found in #5
and #6 and why it does or does not exist.
    
ANSWER: As R's built-in `mean()` probably operates on the same formula
as the one I used, there is no difference between the two means.
